question.problem:
| $x$ | $-8$ | $-4$ | $-2$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.3$ | $0.3$ | $0.3$ | $0.1$ |

Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{60}$ be a random sample of size $n=60$ from a population with the probability mass function given above. Find an approximation for the probability that the sample mean is less than $-4.5.$

*Note: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is 

$$
n=60,
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}f({x}_{i}) \\  & =(-8)\cdot 0.3+(-4)\cdot 0.3+(-2)\cdot 0.3+2\cdot 0.1 \\  & =-2.4-1.2-0.6+0.2 \\  & =-4,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\text{Var}[X] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =((-8)^{2}\cdot 0.3+(-4)^{2}\cdot 0.3+(-2)^{2}\cdot 0.3+{2}^{2}\cdot 0.1)-(-4)^{2} \\  & =(19.2+4.8+1.2+0.4)-16 \\  & =9.6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(-4,\frac{9.6}{60}) \\  & ∼N(-4,0.16).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(\overset{―}{X}<-4.5).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<-4.5) & ≈P(Z<\frac{-4.5-(-4)}{\sqrt{0.16}}) \\  & =P(Z<-1.25) \\  & =Φ(-1.25).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(\overset{―}{X}<-4.5)=Φ(-1.25).
$$
